355956.title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs

scope_fidelity.mathdb_statement: d>1; q ≡ 1 (mod 2d) a power of prime p; r largest with d | (q-1)/(p^r-1); then F_{p^r} is a maximal clique in GP(q,d)=Cay(F_q^+, (F_q^*)^d).
scope_fidelity.primary_text: Identical to Yip, J. Algebraic Combin. 56(2) (2022) 323-333 = arXiv:2101.09652 Conjecture 1.4 (v2 read), and to arXiv:2209.00864 v2 / Algebr. Comb. 6(4) (2023) 901-905 Conjecture 1.1 (arXiv TeX and published ALCO TeX read). Asgarli-Yip arXiv:2106.01522 v2 / JCTA 192 (2022) restates it with the added clause 'F_{p^r} is a subfield of F_q', which is implied by d | (q-1)/(p^r-1) being an integer condition, so equivalent.
scope_fidelity.quantifiers: Universal over d, p, q; the refutation needs one admissible (q,d). q = 5^8, d = 3: q-1 = 390624 ≡ 0 (mod 6); admissible r ∈ {1} only, so r = 1 and the claim is 'F_5 is a maximal clique in GP(5^8,3)'.
scope_fidelity.metadata_note: MathDB status field is 'open'. Its references field carries a mis-attached quote ('Status: solved according to the source') which concerns the Peisert-graph analogue confirmed by Asgarli-Yip, not this conjecture. The statement text itself says the paper resolves it only 'under a sufficient-size hypothesis'.

ordinary_mathematics.script: scripts/yip_verify.py (own GF(5^8) arithmetic; no shared code); log logs/yip-verify.log; output checks/yip-verify.json; 1.9 s under 2 CPU / 6 GiB / 120 s caps
facts_verified: f = X^8+X^7+2X^6+2 is irreducible over F_5 (X has Frobenius orbit length 8)
-1 and all of F_5^* are cubes (F_5 is a clique; graph undirected)
x = 2θ+4θ^2+θ^3 ∉ F_5 and x-a is a nonzero cube for a = 0..4 (direct exponentiation (x-a)^((q-1)/3) = 1)
F_5 ⊕ xF_5 is a 25-clique (all 24 nonzero a+bx are cubes), as predicted by Yip's Lemma 2.1 (JACO 2022)
generators of F_25^* and F_625^* are non-cubes, so F_5 is also a maximal SUBFIELD clique (Theorem 1.2's hypothesis structure, minus q>(n-1)^2)
exhaustive: exactly 960 extension vertices, all of degree 8 over F_5 (log-table count, consistent with direct exponentiation)
ordinary_mathematics.consistency_with_source_computations: No extension vertex lies in F_625; since GP(5^8,3) restricted to F_625 is GP(625,3) (626 ≡ 2 mod 3), this agrees with Yip's reported SageMath verification for n ≤ 5 (here n = 4, q = 5). The counterexample needs n = 8, outside both Yip's checks (n ≤ 5; n = 6 with q ≤ 17) and Theorem 1.2 (5 ≤ (8-1)^2 = 49). No theorem in the read literature is contradicted (Prop. cliquenumber2 of arXiv:2304.13213 needs q < d|K|(|K|+1) = 90, false here).

novelty.basis: All primary follow-ups by the conjecture's author treat it as confirmed or proved within range; the 2025 DCC paper restates it as proved; no registry entry; web search negative.

reasons: Refutes, in exact universal scope, a published conjecture (JACO 2022, Conj. 1.4) that its author's follow-up (ALCO 2023) announces as 'confirmed'/'resolved' and that a later published paper (DCC 2025) restates as proved without qualification; this corrects the published record, not a wording slip.

Also refutes the explicit remark-conjecture of ALCO 2023 that the hypothesis q > (n-1)^2 can be dropped from Theorem 1.2 (F_5 is a maximal subfield clique that is not a maximal clique), showing that some size hypothesis is genuinely necessary for GP, the case the source distinguished from GP*, where it exhibited failures.

Not a routine corollary: no known theorem implies it; the source's own exhaustive checks (n ≤ 5; n = 6, q ≤ 17) did not find it; it first occurs at n = 8 with q = 390625, outside the obvious first tests. The author's sweep (q ≤ 5·10^6, 219 open-range cases) found only this one.

Not a parameter instance in the excluded sense: a single admissible (q,d) is a complete negative resolution of the universal conjecture; not a domain/endpoint correction (the hypotheses q ≡ 1 mod 2d, d>1 hold literally).
Mathematical content beyond the finite check: it gives ω(GP(5^8,3)) ≥ 25 via a 2-dimensional F_5-subspace clique, contradicting the 'tempting' ω = |K| heuristic of DCC 2025.
adversarial_points_considered: The existence of counterexamples for the GP* analogue (ALCO remark) makes a GP failure plausible a posteriori; the source nonetheless conjectured the opposite for GP specifically.

Theorem 1.2 covers p^r > (n-1)^2, i.e. most large-subfield cases; the counterexample lives in the regime the source admitted was unproven. This bounds but does not remove significance, because the source asserted the unrestricted conjecture and claimed it confirmed.
The q ≤ 5·10^6 sweep and 'only failure' claim is author diagnostic data, not part of the result; I re-verified only (5^8,3).

355956.recommendation: Eligible for root acceptance on source fidelity, novelty (bounded) and significance. Present the paper as a counterexample to Yip's Conjecture 1.4 (= ALCO Conj. 1.1) and to the ALCO remark-conjecture, noting explicitly that Theorem 1.2 is not contradicted (5 ≤ 49) and that the published abstract's 'confirms' and the DCC 2025 restatement overstate what was proved. Cite the 25-clique F_5 ⊕ xF_5.
